name: Richard Bergmann
summary: World singles champion for Austria in 1937 and for England in 1939, 1948 and 1950, noted above all for his defence, from the era when defence was a route to the very top.

name: Tong Ling
summary: Won the women's world singles title as a defender in Novi Sad in 1981.

name: Chen Xinhua
summary: Chinese defender who won the World Cup in 1985 and represented England from 1990.

name: Ding Song
summary: Chopped with backspin, then attacked with his forehand. In the 1995 men's team final in Tianjin he beat Peter Karlsson as China beat Sweden 3-2.

name: Koji Matsushita
summary: Japan's leading chopper of his generation, whose name is still on Butterfly's defensive blades used by Han Ying, Linda Bergström and Wang Yang.

name: Chen Weixing
summary: Born in Inner Mongolia in 1972, he became one of Austria's mainstays as an attacking chopper, winning European doubles gold in 2003 and team gold in 2015.

name: Evgueni Chtchetinine
summary: Minsk-born defender who reached No 47 in the world and played for Belarus alongside Vladimir Samsonov.

name: Joo Se-hyuk
summary: The defining modern men's chopper: world singles runner-up in 2003, the first defender to win a men's Pro Tour singles title since Ding Song when he took the Korean Open in 2006, and still world No 8 in 2010.

name: Kim Kyung-ah
summary: Olympic singles bronze medallist in Athens in 2004 and world No 5 in 2010.

name: Hou Yingchao
summary: At 39, beat the young Wang Chuqin 4-0 to win the 2019 Chinese national title, 19 years after his first, the oldest national champion China has had.

name: Park Mi-young
summary: Formed a defensive doubles pair with Kim Kyung-ah that won Olympic team bronze in Beijing in 2008, took world doubles bronze in 2007, 2009 and 2011, and reached No 8 in the world.

name: Yuka Ishigaki
summary: Nagoya-born chopper who won world team silver with Japan in 2014, reached No 19 in the world and retired in 2018.

name: Masato Shiono
summary: Ranked 188th, the 27-year-old defender paid his own entry fees and won the 2013 Japan Open, beating three top-30 players including Chuang Chih-Yuan.

name: Li Qian
summary: Baoding-born defender who played four Olympics for Poland, won the European singles title in 2018 and world doubles bronze in 2015, and retired in 2024.

name: Wu Yang
summary: World junior champion in 2009 whose chopping took her to No 4 in the world.

name: Suh Hyo-won
summary: South Korea's chopper of the 2010s, held up by Butterfly's coaches as a model of the modern women's defender.

name: Ri Myong Sun
summary: North Korean defender who reached No 20 in the world in 2014, won world team bronze in 2016 and played two Olympics.

name: Kim Song-i
summary: Beat Ai Fukuhara 4-1 for Olympic singles bronze in Rio in 2016; the ITTF called her stout in defence and more varied than her fellow defender Ri Myong Sun.
